**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verses 5–10:**

﴿By those who bring down the Reminder﴾. He means the angels, who convey the Reminder (dhikr) to the prophets. A parallel is His saying: "He sends down the Spirit by His command" [Ghafir: 15].

﴿As an excuse or a warning﴾. That is, for the purpose of establishing proof (i'dhar) and warning (inedhar). Al-Hasan recited "ʿudhran" with a dhamma on the dhal (ʿudhuran), and it is disputed how this is transmitted from Abu Bakr, from ʿAsim. The common reading (qira'at al-ʿamma, the reading of the majority) is with a sukun (sukun, absence of vowel) on the dhal. Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read both "ʿudhran" and "nudhran" with a sukun on the dhal in both words. The rest read them with a dhamma. Whoever reads with a sukun says: because the two words are in the place of verbal nouns (masdar) meaning "warning" and "establishing proof", and they are not plurals, so their vowel is not moved (to a dhamma). Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Ibn ʿAmir, Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, and Ya'qub according to the transmission of Ruways ibn Hassan read "ʿudhran" with a sukun on the dhal and "nudhuran" with a dhamma on the dhal. Rawh read both "ʿudhuran" and "nudhuran" with a dhamma, and this is the reading of al-Hasan. The reasoning behind both is that ʿudhur and nudhur, with two dhammas, like udhun (ear) and ʿunuq (neck), is the original form, and it is permissible to lighten them, just as it is permissible to lighten ʿunuq and udhun. It is said: ʿudhr and nudhr, and ʿudhur and nudhur, just as it is said: ʿunq and ʿunuq, and udhn and udhur. The words ʿudhr and nudhr are verbal nouns meaning "establishing proof" and "warning", like nakir, ʿadhir and nadhir. It is also permissible that they are plurals of ʿadhir and nadhir. It is also permissible that ʿudhur is the plural of ʿadhir, like sharif and shurf. The meaning is one and the same whether the vowel is moved or left still, as we have explained up to this point.

These are the oaths which he mentioned before His saying: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾, concerning the matter of the Hour and the Resurrection, ﴿is surely going to occur﴾ [that is, will certainly happen]. Then he mentioned when it will occur, saying: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾, that is, their light is erased.

﴿And when the sky is split open﴾, that is, cleft.

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾, that is, uprooted from their places.

The reasoning behind both is that ʿudhur and nudhur, with two dhammas, like udhun (ear) and ʿunuq (neck), is the original form, and it is permissible to lighten them, just as it is permissible to lighten ʿunuq and udhun. Others read "جِمَالَاتٌ" (jimālāt), with an alif and a kasrah on the jīm, as the plural of "الْجِمَالُ" (al-jimāl, ropes). Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are the ropes of ships, some joined to others until they become like the middles of men. ﴿ṣufr﴾ [yellow] is the plural of "الْأَصْفَرُ" (al-aṣfar, yellow), meaning the colour of fire. It was also said that "الصُّفْرُ" (aṣ-ṣufr) means black, because a ḥadīth states: "Indeed the sparks of the fire of Hell are black like tar" (al-qīr). The Arabs call black camels "ṣufr" because some yellowness mingles with their blackness, just as white gazelles are called "adam", because their whiteness is overlaid with a dullness.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers, this is a day when they will not speak﴾. On the Day of Resurrection there are stations: in some of them they dispute and speak, and in some of them a seal is placed upon their mouths, so they do not speak.

﴿Nor will they be permitted to offer excuses﴾. It is in the nominative case, coordinated with His saying "يُؤْذَنُ" (yu'dhanu, is permitted). Al-Junayd said: meaning there is no excuse for one who turns away from his Benefactor and disbelieves in His favours and blessings.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers, this is the Day of Judgement﴾, between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. ﴿We have gathered you and the former peoples﴾, meaning the deniers of this nation and the former peoples who denied their prophets.

﴿So if you have a stratagem, then use it against Me﴾. Muqatil said: if you have a plan, then devise for yourselves.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers. Indeed the righteous will be among shades﴾, the plural of "ظِلٌّ" (ẓill), meaning in the shade of trees, ﴿and springs﴾ of water.

﴿And fruits of what they desire﴾.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 77, verses 43–50:

It will be said to them, ﴿Eat and drink with ease for what you used to do﴾ in the world, by obeying Me.

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾

Then He said to the disbelievers of Makkah: ﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little﴾ in the world, ﴿indeed you are criminals﴾, polytheists who associate others with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and who deserve the punishment.

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Woe on that Day to the deniers. And when it is said to them, "Bow down"﴾ — that is, pray — ﴿they do not bow down﴾, meaning they do not pray. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) said: this is said to them on the Day of Resurrection, when they are called to prostration and are unable to do so.

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers. So in what statement after this﴾ — after the Qur'an — ﴿will they believe?﴾ — since they do not believe in it.
